definition: Physical hardening and hazard protection modify the engineering, materials or physical configuration of project-financed infrastructure so that it can withstand an identified climate or disaster hazard. Counts when the project finances, builds, retrofits or explicitly requires concrete protective measures such as elevation, flood barriers, drainage, waterproofing, reinforced foundations, wind-resistant structures, heat-resistant components or protective enclosures. The defining intervention is a physical engineering change: selecting a less-exposed location belongs to climate_informed_siting, assessing the hazard belongs to cra, alternative communications paths belong to network_redundancy, and backup electricity belongs to backup_power. A generic requirement for infrastructure to be resilient is insufficient unless an identifiable engineering or protection measure is specified. Does not count for ordinary engineering standards, routine maintenance, reconstruction without an identifiable resilience improvement, or generic references to resilient, robust or climate-resilient infrastructure. Laying a cable underground instead of on poles is a deployment choice that belongs to climate_informed_siting; protective ducts, conduits, armouring and enclosures for cables belong here. Environmental and social instruments that mention resilience in general do not count. The sentence must name a specific engineering measure applied to a named asset: generic wording such as "climate-resilient construction" or "resiliency standards" is grade 1. Drainage or flood control built as the project's own investment is not hardening of an asset. Data-centre tier standards (Uptime Tier III, Tier IV and similar) are backup_power.
boundary: The project changes how infrastructure is physically engineered to withstand risk.
note: Keep the existing id for continuity, but use the narrower name.
